decision.text: D1: CARRIER. A 'personal' message to 'cc' through cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py RemoteBus.post. Measured 2026-10-27: bus.post fires delivery only for 'personal'; 'announce' reaches no subscriber and the bus has no subscribe. Akien's words: 'a message to your bus address'. The address 'cc' is one module constant, so moving to subscription later changes one line.

D6: HANDLER LIST, superseding D1's single address. Akien 2026-10-27: 'each device can add probes to a gate, so it probably makes sense for the list of probes in this case to be a list of handlers and data to give them as opposed to probes that are compiled in to pieces of python.' Certification reads a list of entries {to: <bus address>, verb, data} and posts one 'personal' envelope to each, the body being D3's fields plus that entry's data. No trigger or carry callables: the certification is the trigger. Today the list holds one entry, to 'cc', verb 'certified'. Where the list lives and how a device adds itself is open-question-bound.
